17G.13 Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.

precepts.text: I will mar the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem, this evil people which refuse to hear my words and walk in the imagination of their heart, good for nothing as the girdle. I will dash them one against another and not pity. Hear ye, be not proud, for the Lord hath spoken. Judah followed its treacherous sister into the same pride.
precepts.point: It goes back to Rehoboam, who mocked the elders' counsel and listened to his friends, splitting the kingdom; we are in this condition today because of that pride.
precepts.why:
Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he mocked the leadership above him and dealt with his buddies, and we are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. When you are full of pride you are good for nothing in God's eyes.

Then the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. It can be subtle, shutting down, thinking you can do it on your own, and Satan still has you there.

precepts.text: As the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear; our very life cleaves to the Most High, yet the people followed the religions instead.
precepts.point: Who blesses everybody that does not keep the commandments and still gets everything they desire? Satan says come as you are; whoever wants power, fame, and money in this world without obeying God can have it from him, and you will pay the piper when you meet Christ. Share these precepts with your family.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“For as the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man, so have I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, saith the Lord; that they might be unto me for a people, and for a name, and for a praise, and for a glory: but they would not hear.”

Our very life cleaves to the Most High, as the girdle cleaves to the loins of a man; yet the people followed the religions instead, and would not hear. That is forgetting the Lord thy God, “for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant”: the power belongs to the covenant, to the people that cleave unto him. Keep no commandments and boast of what thine own hand has gotten, and it was not God blessing you.

precepts.text: Can the Ethiopian change his skin or the leopard his spots? The Ethiopians are the dark nations of people; change does not just up and happen, so neither can you do good who are accustomed to do evil.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure because the prophecies in this Bible are sure; we have a more sure word of prophecy. Did we not go into slavery on ships like the Most High declared through Moses in Deuteronomy 28? We are living proof that the Bible is real.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
The law converts the soul, because you do not just up and decide to follow the Bible. “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may ye also do good, that are accustomed to do evil.”

The Ethiopians are the dark nations of people. Can they change their skin, or the leopard his spots? Change does not just up and happen, so neither can you do good who are accustomed to do evil. It takes conversion, and it is the law of the Lord that converts the soul.

points: The Most High tells Jeremiah to get a linen girdle, put it on his loins, and not put it in water. After wearing it he is sent to hide it by the Euphrates, in the area of Iraq.
After many days he is told to go dig it up, and behold the girdle was marred and profitable for nothing.
After this manner the Most High will mar the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem, an evil people who refuse to hear His words and walk after other gods.

There was a punishment for us going into idolatry and sin, and for being so prideful that we started to forget the Most High is in control of everything. Just as that girdle was good for nothing, the nation of Israel became the same way.
As the girdle cleaves to the loins of a man, the Most High caused the whole house of Israel and Judah to cleave to Him for a name and a praise, but they would not hear.

Every bottle shall be filled with wine, and the Most High will fill all the inhabitants of the land, even the kings on David's throne and the priests and prophets, with drunkenness, and dash them one against another.

He will smash the fathers and the sons together and will not pity nor spare nor have mercy. That is why there is such a big discrepancy in the black community between fathers and sons: sons grow without fathers, become fathers, and grow without their children. It is a repeating cycle.

Be not proud; give glory to the Most High before He causes darkness and your feet stumble on the dark mountains. If you will not hear, His soul weeps in secret places because the flock is carried away captive.
The king and queen are told to humble themselves and sit down, for their principalities and crown shall come down, and Judah shall be wholly carried away captive.
Judah is asked what she will say when punished, for she taught her enemies to be captains over her, and sorrows will take her like a woman in travail.

Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Then may you also do good who are accustomed to do evil. The people of Ethiopia are very dark; the land is named the land of burnt faces, and they cannot get lighter. In the same way you cannot hide the evil that you do.
Because she forgot the Most High and trusted in falsehood, He will scatter them as stubble and discover their skirts upon their face so their shame appears.
He has seen the adulteries, the lewdness of the whoredoms, and the abominations. We see it day to day, and there is going to be a judgment for all of it.
